sections.h2: Support per kWh fell from ₹9,400 approved in 2023 to ₹1,576 in 2026

chart.title: Each round pays less per kWh, but the 2026 rate is only an average
chart.sub: Government support per kWh of storage, ₹.
chart.source: Cabinet and MoP decisions; 2026 is an average.

sections.means: Support per kWh has dropped as battery prices fell, but the 2026 figure averages three technologies and is not a battery rate.
sections.todo: Ask for the battery and pumped-storage split of the ₹14,500 crore, since the release does not give it.

sections.h2: Of the 2023 battery scheme's 12.7 GWh signed, only 0.5 GWh is commissioned

chart.title: Most signed battery capacity has not reached commissioning
chart.sub: GWh of battery energy storage by stage, as of July 2026.

sections.means: VGF is paid in stages, so low payments partly reflect timing, but commissioned capacity is still a small share of what was signed.
sections.todo: Report commissioned GWh and rupees paid alongside sanctioned figures for each VGF round, so the next scheme is judged on delivery.

sections.h2: Domestic cell output is about 1.4 GWh against 40 GWh awarded under ACC

chart.title: Commissioned cell capacity is a fraction of the 40 GWh awarded
chart.sub: GWh of lithium-ion cell capacity under the ACC PLI scheme.
chart.source: ACC PLI figures as cited in the post.

sections.means: Domestic cell output is a small fraction of the awarded capacity, so the 40% content rule could bind on imported cells.
sections.todo: Define how the 40% domestic-content floor is measured, since the release leaves that open, before bids close.

sections.h2: The supported pipeline reaches 44% of the 411 GWh needed by 2031-32

chart.title: Storage in place and in the pipeline still leaves about 231 GWh short
chart.sub: GWh of storage: installed, pipeline and total if all is built.

sections.means: Installed storage plus the undelivered pipeline reaches about 180 GWh, which is 44% of the 411 GWh needed.
sections.todo: Remove overlaps from the 180 GWh total and track commissioned GWh each year against the roughly 18 GWh a year the scheme needs.
